title: Unit-compatible section maps satisfy the functor and cocone laws.
statement: Let $J$ be a small category and $F:J\to\mathrm{Cat}$ a diagram of small categories [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Let $P_j$ be a precoverage on $F(j)$, let $V$ be a cocone with vertex $C$, and let $Q$ be a precoverage on $C$. Assume every transition $F(a)$ and every $V_j$ is continuous for the generated topologies [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Fix $i\in J$, a set-valued sheaf $G$ on $P_i$, and $U\in F(i)$. For $t=(i\to j)$ in $\mathrm{Under}(i)$ put $G_t=F(t.hom)_sG$, $S_t=G_t(F(t.hom)U)$, $H=V_{i,s}G$, and $T=H(V_iU)$. Write $\eta_t$ and $\eta_i^V$ for the inverse-image adjunction units. Suppose sheaf maps $\alpha_t:G_t\to V_j^sH$ and $\theta_b:G_t\to F(b.right)^sG_{t'}$ are given for each $b:t\to t'$, and for every $X\in F(i)$ their composites with $\eta_t(X)$ equal $\eta_i^V(X)$ and $\eta_{t'}(X)$, respectively, as objects of the arrow category. Suppose functions $m_b:S_t\to S_{t'}$ and $c_t:S_t\to T$ equal the evaluated $\theta_b$ and $\alpha_t$ as arrow objects (so endpoint identifications are included). Then $m_{\mathrm{id}_t}=\mathrm{id}_{S_t}$, $m_{b'b}=m_{b'}m_b$, and $c_{t'}m_b=c_t$. No category-colimit, filteredness, or covering-finiteness assumption is required.

proof.text: The private set-valued helper sheaf_unit_unique applies the injective hom equivalence of sheafAdjunctionContinuous. Equality of the unit composites as Arrow objects gives equality of presheaf components by Arrow.mk_inj, hence equality of natural transformations and sheaf maps. No conjugate isomorphism is needed.

proof.text: The private helpers sheaf_triangle_id and sheaf_triangle_comp substitute the strict functor equalities, and compare unit composites. For identity compare with the identity natural transformation; for composition use associativity and the two unit equations, then uniqueness. In the main proof F.map_id, F.map_comp and Under.w give the transition triangles; V.w gives the triangles for the limit legs. These yield the evaluated Arrow equalities hid, hcomp and hcone at arbitrary stage objects.

proof.text: Define concrete section maps mm and k by evaluating theta and alpha and composing with eqToHom of the endpoint equalities. Arrow.arrow_mk_comp_eqToHom removes the terminal transports in Arrow equalities. For composition and cocone naturality, use naturality of theta and alpha at eqToHom of the stage-object equality to move the middle transport across the later component; use eqToHom_map and associativity. This proves hmm_id, hmm_comp and hk. The hypotheses hm and hc and Arrow.mk_injective identify the given m and c with mm and k, respectively. Rewrite by these identifications to conclude all three laws.

theorem colimit_site_set_section_coherence
    (J : Type u) [SmallCategory J] (F : J ⥤ Cat.{u, u})
    (P : ∀ j : J, Precoverage (F.obj j))
    [∀ (j k : J) (a : j ⟶ k),
      (F.map a).toFunctor.IsContinuous (P j).toGrothendieck (P k).toGrothendieck]
    (V : Cocone F)
    (Q : Precoverage V.pt)
    [∀ j : J, (V.ι.app j).toFunctor.IsContinuous
      (P j).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck]
    (i : J) (G : Sheaf (P i).toGrothendieck (Type u))
    (α : ∀ t : Under i,
                (sheafPullback (F.map t.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
                  (P i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).obj G ⟶
                ((V.ι.app t.right).toFunctor.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u)
                  (P t.right).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).obj
                  ((sheafPullback (V.ι.app i).toFunctor (Type u)
                    (P i).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).obj G))
    (hα : (∀ (t : Under i) (X : F.obj i),
                  Arrow.mk (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (F.map t.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
                    (P i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).unit.app G).hom.app
                      (op X) ≫ (α t).hom.app (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj X))) =
                  Arrow.mk (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (V.ι.app i).toFunctor (Type u)
                    (P i).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).unit.app G).hom.app (op X))))
    (θ : ∀ (t t' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t'),
                        (sheafPullback (F.map t.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
                          (P i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).obj G ⟶
                        ((F.map b.right).toFunctor.sheafPushforwardContinuous (Type u)
                          (P t.right).toGrothendieck (P t'.right).toGrothendieck).obj
                          ((sheafPullback (F.map t'.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
                            (P i).toGrothendieck (P t'.right).toGrothendieck).obj G))
    (hθ : ∀ (t t' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t'),
      (∀ X : F.obj i,
                          Arrow.mk
                            (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (F.map t.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
                              (P i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).unit.app
                                G).hom.app (op X) ≫
                              (θ t t' b).hom.app (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj X))) =
                          Arrow.mk
                            (((sheafAdjunctionContinuous (F.map t'.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
                              (P i).toGrothendieck (P t'.right).toGrothendieck).unit.app
                                G).hom.app (op X))))
    (U : F.obj i)
    (m : ∀ (t t' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t'), ((sheafPullback (F.map t.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
        (P i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).obj G).obj.obj
          (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj U)) ⟶ ((sheafPullback (F.map t'.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
        (P i).toGrothendieck (P t'.right).toGrothendieck).obj G).obj.obj
          (op ((F.map t'.hom).toFunctor.obj U)))
    (c : ∀ t : Under i, ((sheafPullback (F.map t.hom).toFunctor (Type u)
        (P i).toGrothendieck (P t.right).toGrothendieck).obj G).obj.obj
          (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj U)) ⟶ ((sheafPullback (V.ι.app i).toFunctor (Type u)
        (P i).toGrothendieck Q.toGrothendieck).obj G).obj.obj
          (op ((V.ι.app i).toFunctor.obj U)))
    (hm : ∀ (t t' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t'),
      Arrow.mk (m t t' b) =
        Arrow.mk ((θ t t' b).hom.app (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj U))))
    (hc : ∀ t : Under i,
      Arrow.mk (c t) =
        Arrow.mk ((α t).hom.app (op ((F.map t.hom).toFunctor.obj U)))) :
    (∀ t : Under i, m t t (𝟙 t) = 𝟙 _) ∧
    (∀ (t t' t'' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t') (b' : t' ⟶ t''),
      m t t'' (b ≫ b') = m t t' b ≫ m t' t'' b') ∧
    (∀ (t t' : Under i) (b : t ⟶ t'), m t t' b ≫ c t' = c t)
